daily_reality.summary: Human factors engineers and ergonomists optimize human-technology interaction by studying usability, safety, and efficiency. They design interfaces, workplaces, and products that account for human capabilities and limitations. Work spans tech, healthcare, defense, and manufacturing.
typical_tasks: Conduct user research and usability testing
Design human-machine interfaces (HMI) and control panels
Perform ergonomic workplace assessments and injury risk analysis
Analyze human error patterns and design error-prevention systems
Develop user requirements and specifications for products/systems
Create task analyses and workflow optimization studies
Apply anthropometric data to product and workspace design
Conduct cognitive task analysis for complex systems
Prepare reports on human performance findings and recommendations
Collaborate with engineering teams on human systems integration (HSI)
key_documents: Ergonomic risk assessments (RULA, REBA, NIOSH Lifting Equation)
Human factors analysis and classification system (HFACS) reports
Safety and incident investigation reports (human factors focus)
Regulatory compliance documentation (FDA human factors for medical devices)

deadlines.fda_submissions: Pre-market submission timelines for medical devices
deadlines.ergonomic_assessments: As needed, often annual for workplace evaluations

daily_reality.seasonality: Generally no strong seasonality. Defense contracting follows government fiscal year. Consumer product cycles may create Q3-Q4 peaks.

regulatory.summary: FDA requires human factors testing for medical devices. OSHA ergonomic guidelines apply to workplace design. CPE certification from BCPE is the gold-standard credential. HFES provides professional standards.

key_laws.name: FDA Human Factors Guidance
key_laws.description: Requires usability testing for medical devices to ensure safe use

key_laws.name: MIL-STD-1472 — Human Engineering
key_laws.description: DoD standard for human factors in defense systems design

key_laws.name: ISO 9241 — Ergonomics of Human-System Interaction
key_laws.description: International standard for usability and user experience

requirements: Graduate degree (MS/PhD) in Human Factors, Ergonomics, or related field
Or bachelor's + 24 semester hours covering specific topics
3 years full-time work experience in the field
certifications: CHFP — Certified Human Factors Professional (Board of Certification)

regulatory.penalties: FDA warning letters and product recalls for inadequate human factors testing. OSHA citations for ergonomic hazards. Product liability for design-related injuries.

tools.summary: Usability testing platforms, eye-tracking systems, motion capture, ergonomic assessment tools, and simulation software for modeling human-system interaction.

primary_tools.name: Eye-tracking systems (Tobii, SMI)
primary_tools.description: Track visual attention during usability studies

primary_tools.name: JACK / Siemens Tecnomatix
primary_tools.description: Digital human modeling for ergonomic simulation

primary_tools.name: RAMSIS
primary_tools.description: Automotive ergonomic design and occupant packaging

primary_tools.name: Morae / UserZoom / Lookback
primary_tools.description: Usability testing and user research platforms

primary_tools.name: Motion capture systems
primary_tools.description: Track body movements for ergonomic assessment

primary_tools.name: Statistical software (SPSS, R, JMP)
primary_tools.description: Experimental data analysis for human factors research

secondary_tools: RULA/REBA/NIOSH calculators for ergonomic risk assessment
Figma / Sketch / Adobe XD for interface prototyping
SolidWorks / CAD for product design review
Force gauges and EMG for biomechanical measurement
Survey tools (Qualtrics, SurveyMonkey) for user research
VR/AR headsets for immersive prototype testing
pain_points: Difficulty quantifying ROI of human factors work to stakeholders
Being included too late in the design process
Balancing user needs with engineering and business constraints
Recruiting representative participants for usability studies

terminology.summary: Blends engineering, psychology, and design terminology with ergonomic assessment methods and human performance metrics.

terms.HFACS: Human Factors Analysis and Classification System
terms.RULA: Rapid Upper Limb Assessment — ergonomic risk tool
terms.REBA: Rapid Entire Body Assessment — ergonomic risk tool
terms.NIOSH Lifting Equation: Tool for assessing manual material handling risk
terms.anthropometry: Study of human body measurements for design
terms.affordance: Design property suggesting how an object should be used
terms.cognitive load: Amount of mental effort required to perform a task
terms.situation awareness: Understanding of the current environment and task state
terms.Fitts' Law: Model predicting time to reach a target based on size and distance
terms.heuristic evaluation: Expert review of interface against usability principles
terms.think-aloud protocol: User verbalization method during usability testing
terms.BCPE: Board of Certification in Professional Ergonomics

career_psychology.summary: Growing specialty with salary range $91K-$132K+ (or higher in tech). Rapid growth of 9.7% projected. Intellectually diverse work combining psychology, engineering, and design. CPE certification increasingly important.
career_path: Bachelor's degree in Human Factors, Psychology, Industrial Engineering, or related field
Master's or PhD in Human Factors / Ergonomics (preferred for most positions)
Director of UX / Human Factors / Ergonomics
fears: Design decisions leading to user errors and injuries
Work being deprioritized or cut from project budgets
Difficulty demonstrating impact to engineering leadership
Keeping up with rapidly evolving technology interfaces
FDA audit findings for medical device usability
motivation: Making technology and workplaces safer and more usable
Interdisciplinary work blending psychology, design, and engineering
Direct impact on user safety and satisfaction
Growing recognition and demand for human-centered design
burnout_factors: Advocating for user needs against tight schedules and budgets
Repetitive testing cycles with incremental improvements
Being a lone HF specialist on large engineering teams
Documentation and regulatory compliance demands (medical devices)
Travel requirements for on-site ergonomic assessments

community.summary: Primary community centered around HFES (3,500 members in 58 countries) and BCPE for certification. Strong academic and applied research community.

associations.name: Human Factors and Ergonomics Society (HFES)
associations.description: 3,500+ members, 58 countries, founded 1957, world's largest HF/E society

associations.name: Board of Certification in Professional Ergonomics (BCPE)
International Ergonomics Association (IEA)
associations.description: Global federation of ergonomics/human factors societies

associations.name: Association for Computing Machinery SIGCHI
associations.description: Special interest group on human-computer interaction

online_communities: LinkedIn Human Factors and Ergonomics groups
conferences: HFES Annual Meeting — primary professional conference
ACM CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing

market.summary: Growing field with 9.7% projected job growth, driven by technology complexity, medical device regulation, and workplace safety focus. Strong salary potential especially in tech sector. 25,100 new jobs projected by 2026.
market.growth_rate: 9.7% above national average, 25,100 new jobs projected
top_employers: Medical device companies (FDA human factors requirements)
Consulting firms (Exponent, Human Factors Research Group)
market_trends: FDA human factors requirements driving medical device demand
Autonomous vehicles and AI systems requiring HFE expertise
Remote work ergonomics creating new consulting opportunities
Increasing regulatory focus on human factors in safety-critical systems
AR/VR interaction design opening new specialization paths
